_: The bank. Every rule in this studio started as a row here, and each row names the check that now enforces it. Seed these into the lessons table on project creation — a rule with a scar attached gets followed; an invented best-practice does not.

lessons.title: Identity drift from unbound characters
lessons.what_came_back: The same man rendered as different people across neighbouring shots — different face, different age, different jacket.
lessons.why: One shot named <Tom> and bound him to a reference sheet; the next said 'the man in the navy parka' and bound him to nothing. The route did exactly as told.
lessons.fix: Every character is defined ONCE in a cast/passport record and every shot resolves against it. A shot cannot describe a character in its own words.
lessons.general_rule: The model has no memory, so the pipeline is the memory. One asset, one passport, copied verbatim, never shortened.

lessons.title: The undirected face
lessons.what_came_back: A man smiling warmly through three consecutive shots about his grandmother's broken heirloom; scripted 'faintest dry amusement' rendered as a broad grin.
lessons.why: Body was directed, voice was directed, the mouth was directed — and the expression was left unstated, so the model filled the silence with the average of every warm scene it has seen, which is 'pleasant'.
lessons.fix: assets.default_expression plus a per-shot override, and where the beat needs it, the words 'not smiling'.
lessons.general_rule: Direct every channel the audience can read — body, voice, mouth AND face — or the model directs it toward the middle.

lessons.title: Approval outlived the set
lessons.what_came_back: The one approved take in a scene was shot in a room that no longer existed — and survived a full day as 'done' precisely because it was the one shot everybody trusted.
lessons.why: A skip flag was doing two jobs and only one honestly: exempt from re-firing is not exempt from canon. Sixteen individual reviews missed it; one contact sheet caught it in four seconds.
lessons.fix: The downstream invalidation graph: a plate, lock, sheet or script change marks every downstream approval provisional. Nothing is deleted; approved becomes provisional. And scenes are reviewed on ONE contact sheet, never shot by shot.
lessons.general_rule: An approval is stamped against a state of the world, not against a file.

lessons.title: Describing what the frame does not show is an instruction to build it
lessons.what_came_back: A tight insert of a counter top pulled back and invented a bright kitchen with a window in it, two stops cooler than the shots either side.
lessons.why: Every prompt opened by reciting the whole room. On a frame showing only a counter top that is a list of things NOT in the picture, and a model that must render something behind the counter had just been told what. The keyframe was not ignored — it was completed.
lessons.fix: shots.room_scope (full/partial/none) scopes the scene clause to what the frame shows, and an insert carries a framing lock: never widens, never pulls back, nothing beyond Image 1 becomes visible.
lessons.general_rule: A prompt is a list of things the model may draw. The test before any scene clause: is this visible in the frame? On a tight frame, say so explicitly — silence is a gap too.

lessons.title: The wrong mouth
lessons.what_came_back: One man's recorded line animated onto the other man's face — twice, at two different pipeline stages.
lessons.why: First: an unassigned mouth in the prompt moves. Second: the lipsync service never sees the prompt, and no route measured accepts a face selector — on a two-shot it finds a face and drives it.
lessons.fix: In the prompt: every mouth in frame assigned, speaker open, all others closed-but-never-frozen. At sync: a speaker_box crops to the speaker alone; crop, upscale, sync, composite back at the same coordinates.
lessons.general_rule: The speaker law must reach every stage that can move a mouth, including the ones that cannot read the prompt.

lessons.title: The audit that belonged to a different text
lessons.what_came_back: A prompt materially rewritten — seven new reference bindings and a different route — fired against the audit of the version before the change. Later, a passing score was recorded on identical words that had just failed.
lessons.why: A stamp records that an audit happened; it does not force the loop when one fails. A correction produces a NEW text that has never been scored.
lessons.fix: Audit rounds stamped against a sha256 of the exact text. Only a round matching the current hash counts. A pass on text whose latest round failed requires an explicit override.
lessons.general_rule: The audit is a loop, not a stamp, and it runs until the floor is cleared on the CURRENT words.

lessons.title: Dialogue in the prompt of a speech-generating route
lessons.what_came_back: The voice deteriorated mid-take, then a passage arrived completely different — 'a mish-mash mess'. Lip movement could never agree with the recorded line laid over it.
lessons.why: The route generates speech FROM the prompt and animates the mouth to what it invented. Our recording then plays on top; the two can never align.
lessons.fix: No dialogue words in any visual prompt when speech is 'generated'. The mouth is directed as a talking rhythm, the prompt states WHY, and the recording drives articulation in a separate sync pass.
lessons.general_rule: Where the provider invents speech, the words are an audio file, never prompt text.

lessons.title: Numbers for bodies
lessons.what_came_back: Character heights given in centimetres rendered with the ladder inverted — the largest gap drawn as no gap at all.
lessons.why: Models cannot see 118cm. They can see a shoulder.
lessons.fix: assets.scale_landmark holds relationships ('her head reaches his shoulder'). Metres remain fine for location geometry; the ban is on bodies.
lessons.general_rule: Scale by body landmark, never by number.

lessons.title: The sound bed decided the picture length
lessons.what_came_back: A 9-second take assembled at 8 seconds, silently losing the end of its line, because an 8-second room tone ran out and -shortest cut the PICTURE to fit the sound.
lessons.why: Length was inferred from whichever input ran out first instead of stated.
lessons.fix: Beds loop; output length is stated from the shot record. Also: trim the drift at generation edges (the tail especially) and cut harder than feels natural.
lessons.general_rule: State the length; never infer it from an input.

lessons.title: The stale artefact fired as current
lessons.what_came_back: A brief displayed — and fire nearly sent — a prompt file from a superseded grammar that scored -9.5 against the current gate. Separately, 'already shot' skipped a take made from a completely different prompt.
lessons.why: Reading artefacts off disk trusts that the world has not moved since they were written.
lessons.fix: Brief and fire compile FRESH at the moment of use. Takes carry the hash of the prompt that made them; a skip requires a hash match.
lessons.general_rule: Never trust a stored artefact to represent the current state — recompute or hash-check at the point of use.
lessons.enforced_by: fresh compile + take prompt-hash stamp / idempotency key

lessons.title: The keyframe pipeline
lessons.what_came_back: The first shot in the production where the voice on the track and the mouth on the screen were the same performance — approved on sight.
lessons.why: A human-generated keyframe as Image 1 (roled as the complete opening composition), appearance sheets behind it, an audited prose prompt with no dialogue, sync from the recording inside a speaker box, sound laid under at assembly.
lessons.general_rule: Human keyframe → audited prose prompt ≥ floor → reference-to-video with the frame as Image 1 → sync inside a speaker box → bed. Generate keyframes per SETUP and chain the end frame for everything else.

lessons.title: The stress test pays for itself on cell one
lessons.what_came_back: The very first live stress still surfaced the character's default faint smile — the exact NEG-002 fault — in a cheap still instead of three video renders.
lessons.why: Sheets travel as references on EVERY shot, so an untested sheet is a fault multiplied by every shot the character appears in.
lessons.general_rule: Prove every passport under combat conditions — angles, sizes, the scene's own light, a two-shot beside every co-star — before a frame of video is paid for.
lessons.enforced_by: stress gate: no pass, no lock

lessons.title: Deterministic hero sound
lessons.what_came_back: A plot-critical sound ('the same notes are wrong every single time') built note-by-note in code, so the wrongness is a table and is identical on every repeat — where a generative model returned a different wrongness every run.
lessons.why: When the script asserts a repeatable property of a sound or prop, generation cannot promise it.
lessons.general_rule: If the plot depends on a property being exact and repeatable, synthesise it deterministically; do not generate it.
